topic: The Essence of Calculus: From Discrete to Continuous
target_audience: High school students or introductory university students

sections.title: The Hook: The Limits of Measuring Change
lecture_lines: Measuring average speed is simple.
But what is speed at an instant?
Think of a cheetah chasing a gazelle.

sections.title: Prerequisite Concept: The Power of Zooming In
lecture_lines: Zooming into a curve reveals its path.
Small segments eventually look like straight lines.
This is our window to local analysis.

sections.title: The Derivative: The Science of 'Right Now'
lecture_lines: The derivative measures change right now.
It shows the slope at every point.
Like a speedometer tracking instant velocity.
Visualize a line sliding along the curve.
Calculus captures this fleeting, dynamic reality.

sections.title: The Integral: Reconstructing the Whole
lecture_lines: Integration reconstructs wholes from tiny slices.
It sums infinitely small parts together.
Like filling a reservoir, slice by slice.
We accumulate change to find the total.
The integral is an engine of reconstruction.

sections.title: Conclusion: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
lecture_lines: Derivatives and integrals are inverse processes.
Two sides of one beautiful coin.
They bridge snapshots and dynamic motion.
This is the fundamental theorem of calculus.
Understanding change gives us the world.
